summary.title: Hack The Virtual Memory: C strings & /proc
summary.one_liner: You learn how to find and overwrite a C string in the heap of a running Linux process by reading /proc/[pid]/maps and /proc/[pid]/mem.
takeaways: Each process has its own virtual memory; the stack sits at high addresses and the heap at low addresses.
/proc/[pid]/maps lists mapped regions, including the [heap] range and its permissions.
/proc/[pid]/mem can be opened and seeked to read or write memory inside a running process (as root).
A short Python 3 script can locate a string in the heap and overwrite it with a string of the same or shorter length.
summary.summary: This first chapter of the Holberton "Hack The Virtual Memory" series explains virtual memory basics, including the high-address stack and low-address heap layout. It then uses a small C program that calls strdup, a loop program that prints the duplicated string, and the /proc filesystem to inspect the process. The author reads /proc/[pid]/maps to find the heap range, then uses a Python 3 script to search /proc/[pid]/mem and overwrite "Holberton" with "Fun w vm!" in the running process. The tested environment is Ubuntu 14.04 with gcc 4.8.4 and Python 3.4.3.
